title: Effects of Extraction Temperature of Protein from Date Palm Pollen on the Astringency Taste of Tea
content: The astringent taste of tea is caused by polyphenols like epigallocatechin gallate (EGCG). This has led to efforts to reduce these compounds in order to make tea products taste better by adding protein. Date palm pollen (DPP) protein has emerged as a promising plant protein source for this purpose. In a recent study, the influence of extraction temperature (30 and 80 °C) on the quality of DPP protein and the astringency taste of tea was investigated. The findings indicated that extraction at 80 °C resulted in increased protein yield and improved surface and thermal properties of DPP.  Spectroscopic methods, such as FTIR, UV, and CD, were used to look at how the structure of the DPP protein changed at 30 and 80 °C with and without EGCG. The results showed that EGCG changed the secondary structures of DPP at 80 °C. A sensory evaluation utilizing quantitative descriptive analysis (QDA) showed a reduction in astringency for DPP-tea polyphenol solutions at 80°C. The food industry stands to benefit from the interaction of tea polyphenols and DPP as a protein-polyphenol complex for a functional beverage that mitigates the astringent taste of tea while preserving its distinctive flavor profile.
